This project studies whether agents express similar semantic content with different rhetorical styles across different submolts (communities). Our pipeline combines dataset preparation, platform-level exploration, topic/narrative discovery, psychographic profiling, and topic-to-trait linkage to produce interpretable evidence about audience-aware language variation. # Research Question Do Moltbook agents adapt their linguistic style when expressing semantically similar ideas across different submolts (communities)? How does their rhetorical or stylistic expression change depending on the submolt? ## Workflow Overview The document is organized as a sequential analysis pipeline: - **Dataset**: source, acquisition, and storage of Moltbook tables. - **General Exploration**: structural analysis of submolts, participation, and activity dynamics. - **Preprocessing**: text normalization and feature preparation. - **Topic and Narrative Discovery**: embedding/community and BERTopic-based theme extraction. - **Psychographic Profiling**: trait/value inference at post and agent levels. - **Linking Topics to Psychographic Traits**: topic-wise trait profiles, correlations, and archetypal examples. # Dataset We use the **Moltbook Observatory Archive** on Hugging Face ([dataset card][hf-moltbook-archive]): an incremental export of the Moltbook Observatory SQLite database, published as date-partitioned Parquet for browsing and programmatic access. Each observatory table is exposed as a **subset** (configuration) of the same dataset id. We load **`agents`**, **`posts`**, **`comments`**, and **`submolts`** for agent metadata, post text and scores, comment text with scores and parent links, and submolt (community) metadata respectively, matching the dataset card. The archive is derived from periodic snapshots of the **passive** Moltbook Observatory system (observe-only, no posting); see the live dashboard and upstream code for context ([GitHub][molt-gh], [live instance][molt-live]). The dataset is published with the **MIT** license. **Attribution.** Dataset and tooling by **Sushant Gautam** and **Michael A.
